model: sig User { follows : set User, sees : set Photo, posts : set Photo, suggested : set User } sig Influencer extends User {} sig Photo { date : one Day } sig Ad extends Photo {} sig Day {}

requirements.description: Every photo is posted by one user

positive.explanation: There are no photos, so every photo is trivially posted by exactly one user.
Photo1 is posted by exactly one user, User1, and has one date.
Photo1 is posted only by User1 and Ad1 is posted only by the influencer Influencer1; each photo has exactly one poster. User2 sees Photo1 and follows Influencer1, which adds no posting.

negative.explanation: Photo1 exists but no user posts it, so it is not posted by one user.
Photo1 is posted by two users, User1 and User2, rather than by one user.
Photo1 is posted by User1, but Photo2 is posted by no user, so Photo2 violates the requirement.

generation.instances:
// There are no photos, so every photo is trivially posted by exactly one user.
run positive1 {
    some disj jsonAtom1 : User |
    {
        User = jsonAtom1
        Influencer = none
        Photo = none
        Ad = none
        Day = none
        User <: follows = none->none
        User <: sees = none->none
        User <: posts = none->none
        User <: suggested = none->none
        Photo <: date = none->none
    }
} for 1 but exactly 1 User, exactly 0 Photo, exactly 0 Day expect 1

        Photo = jsonAtom3

        Day = jsonAtom4
        User <: follows = none->none
        User <: sees = none->none
        User <: posts = jsonAtom1->jsonAtom3
        User <: suggested = none->none
        Photo <: date = jsonAtom3->jsonAtom4
    }
} for 2 but exactly 2 User, exactly 1 Photo, exactly 1 Day expect 1

requirements.description: Users cannot follow themselves

positive.explanation: No users, photos, or days exist, so no user can follow themselves and every photo is posted by exactly one user vacuously.
User1 follows User2, which is not a self-follow. There are no photos, so the posting requirement holds vacuously.
User1 and User2 follow each other, which is allowed because neither follows themselves. Photo1 has exactly one poster (User1) and one date (Day1), and User2 sees it.

negative.explanation: User1 follows User1, which violates the requirement. There are no photos, so the posting requirement still holds.
User2 follows User2, which is a self-follow and violates the requirement. Photo1 still has exactly one poster (User1) and one date (Day1).
Influencer1 follows themselves, which violates the requirement. Photo1 has exactly one poster (User2) and one date (Day1), so the posting requirement holds.

requirements.description: The parts of a component must be assembled before it in the production line

positive.explanation: Component2 (at WSEnd) has Component1 as a part, and Component1 is assembled at WSBegin, which comes earlier in the single line. Component1's other part is a material, so no component part is out of order.

The line is WSBegin, Station1, WSEnd. Component1 (WSBegin) is a part of Component2 (Station1), and Component2 is a part of Component3 (WSEnd). Every component part is assembled strictly earlier than the component it belongs to.

Component3 (WSEnd) has Component1 (WSBegin) as a part, which is earlier in the line. Component3 is dangerous but is assembled only where a robot works, so the danger constraint holds. Component1 and Component2 are assembled at WSBegin with only material parts.

requirements.description: Students working on the same project in a course cannot have marks differing by more than one unit
erroneous:
{
	    all c: Course |
        all p: Project |
            (p in c.projects and 
             some disj s1, s2: Student | 
                (p in s1.projects and p in s2.projects and 
                 ((c.grades[s1] = next[c.grades[s2]]) or 
                  (c.grades[s2] = next[c.grades[s1]]) or 
                  (c.grades[s1] = c.grades[s2]))))
}
